title: 18K vs 22K vs 24K Gold: Which Should You Buy For Jewellery?
excerpt: If you've ever stood at a jewellery counter hearing "18K," "22K," and "24K" thrown around and felt a little lost, you're not alone — this is one of the most common points of confusion for gold buyers in India. The good news: once you understand what karat actually measures, choosing between them becomes a lot simpler.
content:
What Does "Karat" Actually Mean?

Karat measures gold purity on a scale out of 24 — where 24K represents (nearly) pure gold, and lower karat numbers indicate gold mixed with other metals like copper, silver, or zinc. Pure gold is naturally soft, so alloying it with other metals isn't a compromise — it's what makes gold strong enough to actually hold its shape as jewellery.

24K Gold: Maximum Purity, Minimum Durability

24K gold is 99.9% pure gold, marked with the 999 hallmark. It has the richest, deepest yellow colour and the highest gold content of any karat — but that purity comes at a cost: 24K gold is too soft to hold intricate designs or withstand daily wear. This is why 24K gold is typically used for coins, bars, and investment-grade gold rather than jewellery you'd actually wear regularly.

Best for: Investment purchases, gold coins, savings — not everyday jewellery.

22K Gold: The Traditional Indian Standard

22K gold is 91.6% pure, mixed with 8.4% alloy, and hallmarked as 916. This is the gold most traditional Indian jewellery is made from, it keeps the rich, bright yellow tone Indian buyers expect, while being just durable enough to be worked into ornate, traditional designs. It strikes a middle ground: high purity retained, with enough strength added to make it wearable.

Best for: Traditional jewellery, bridal sets, and pieces meant to carry both cultural and resale value.

18K Gold: Built for Everyday Durability

18K gold is 75% pure, mixed with 25% alloy, and hallmarked as 750. It's noticeably more durable than 22K or 24K, which is exactly why it's the preferred choice for diamond and stone-set jewellery — the added strength holds gemstones securely in place, something purer, softer gold struggles to do. It's also the standard used in most Western-style fine jewellery.

Best for: Diamond rings, daily-wear pieces, and designs with intricate stone-setting.

Why the Hallmark Actually Matters

Since June 2021, BIS hallmarking has been mandatory for gold jewellery sold in India, and registered jewellers are required to hallmark gold across all standard karats, including 14K, 18K, 20K, 22K, and 24K. Selling non-hallmarked gold jewellery is a punishable offence — which means the hallmark isn't just a quality nice-to-have, it's your actual proof of purity. Always check for the BIS hallmark and its purity code (999, 916, 750, etc.) before buying, rather than relying on a verbal promise from the seller.

So, Which Should You Actually Buy?

There's no single "best" karat — the right choice depends entirely on what the piece is for:

  • Buying for tradition or a bridal set? Go with 22K — it's the standard for a reason.

  • Buying a diamond or stone-studded piece you'll wear often? 18K holds up better and secures stones more reliably.

  • Buying purely as an investment or store of value? 24K, ideally in coin or bar form rather than jewellery.

Choosing With Confidence at Zoniraz

Whatever karat you choose, the purity claim is only as good as the hallmark backing it. When you're browsing jewellery — at Zoniraz or anywhere else — always check for the BIS hallmark and its purity code before you buy, and ask for clear documentation of the gold's karat, weight, and making charges. That's the real difference between a purchase you can trust and one you're simply taking someone's word for.
